transit.label: Existing network
points: Shows existing metro stops, bus lanes, and the current network structure.
Highlights where transit access is concentrated and where gaps remain.
Sets the baseline used to evaluate later options.

transit.label: Earlier alignment
points: The capstone report describes an earlier route via Honoré-Beaugrand, L’Assomption, and Hochelaga that was rejected in the 2024 PSE study.
The report identifies a narrow right-of-way and frequent driveways on Honoré-Beaugrand.
Steep grades on L’Assomption would require substantial engineering intervention.

transit.label: Proposed alignment
points: The team proposes a route via Hochelaga and Viau in response to the slope and space constraints of the earlier alignment.
A proposed tunnel segment on Viau addresses steeper sections.
The alignment aims to improve east–west access and connect redevelopment areas.
The proposal links transit-oriented development with mobility equity objectives.

slopes.label: Viau Street
points: The profile informed the proposed Viau alignment and tunnel segment.
The 6% line is the reference threshold used in the study.

slopes.label: Assomption Boulevard
points: Sections approach 14% in the study profile.
The comparison highlights where the terrain would require further engineering analysis.

development.label: 3D development
points: Illustrates the proposed block structure and built form arrangement.
Shows how the new layout fits into the surrounding urban fabric.
Highlights the overall development logic before detailing plots and streets.

development.label: Blocks & green space
development.alt: Proposed plots, green spaces, and built form
points: The industrial allotment system is reorganized to introduce finer-grained blocks.
Restructuring improves integration with surrounding residential fabric.
Green spaces are consolidated within blocks for dedicated green infrastructure zones.
Layout supports higher-density, mixed-use development and semi-private open spaces.

development.label: Street hierarchy
points: A new street hierarchy subdivides large industrial parcels and improves walkability.
Key existing streets are retained and integrated into a finer-grained layout.
A shared street intersects Pierre de Coubertin and Hochelaga to enhance pedestrian connectivity.
Proposed streets target a typical width of 28.4 metres to support multimodal access.
